statement: TUBEROUS SCLEROSIS COMPLEX IS AN AMYLOID-INDEPENDENT TAUOPATHY AS WELL AS A DEVELOPMENTAL mTORopathy, AND TSC1 IS IMPLICATED IN ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE ITSELF. The TSC literature describes a two-stage brain phenotype rather than a purely developmental one. Sarnat and Flores-Sarnat 2015 (Brain Dev 37:553) grouped TSC with hemimegalencephaly, focal cortical dysplasia 2 and ganglioglioma as 'infantile tauopathies'. Liu et al. 2020 (JAMA Neurol 77:358) found adults with TSC share cognitive and behavioural features with frontotemporal dementia. Liu et al. 2022 (Acta Neuropathol Commun 10, doi 10.1186/s40478-022-01330-x) reported TSC as a novel AMYLOID-INDEPENDENT tauopathy with elevated phosphorylated 3R/4R tau aggregation, and Hwang et al. 2023 (Acta Neuropathol, doi 10.1007/s00401-022-02521-5) independently described TSC as a novel human tauopathy. Adriaanse et al. 2023 (Neuropathol Appl Neurobiol 49:e12904) reported that TSC1 contributes to selective neuronal vulnerability in Alzheimer's disease. A 2026 preprint (Baumel et al., doi 10.64898/2026.09.09.26362677) reports plasma phosphorylated tau-217 elevated in TSC (n=63) at younger ages than in AD (n=25) or cognitively unimpaired controls (n=116), with a parallel age-related trajectory across the three cohorts.
argument: This is recorded because it CORRECTS an earlier conclusion of mine in this investigation. I had argued that TSC1/TSC2 should not be marked as neurodegeneration-associated on the APOE homeostasis figure, on the grounds that their Open Targets genetic association to MONDO_0005559 ('neurodegenerative disease') is 0.000. That zero is a curation artefact: MONDO indexes tuberous sclerosis as a neoplastic/developmental syndrome, so the ontology does not carry the 2015-2026 tauopathy literature above. The same gene pair scores 4.70 and 4.71 on nervous-system Mendelian evidence, the highest in the figure's gene set. An ontology-derived zero is a statement about indexing, not about biology. WHY IT MATTERS FOR THIS FIGURE: the mTORC1-selective inhibitor drawn as therapeutic hypothesis 2 currently rests only on lysosomal cholesterol, and its own tooltip concedes that every gene in that module is transcriptionally flat in our spatial data. TSC supplies an independent human line of support: an mTOR-hyperactive population with an amyloid-independent tau phenotype and a plasma biomarker to track it. CAVEATS. The 2026 study is a PREPRINT, not peer reviewed, with n=63 TSC. Its own bibliography cites the confound that most threatens it: TSC causes renal angiomyolipomas (Kingswood 2020 TOSCA; Limavady 2024) and renal dysfunction inflates plasma p-tau217 (Janelidze 2023; Yun 2026), so an apparent elevation could be renal rather than cerebral. I have read the abstract and the full bibliography but NOT the results or methods, so I cannot yet say how that adjustment was handled. 'Parallel trajectory shifted younger' is also a narrower claim than TSC causing AD.
